market_holds: Spot about $2.79-2.88 intraday on 2026-11-11 (sealed baseline 2.875 at 18:09 UTC; Yahoo daily bar 2.79). The front-expiry (Nov 13) straddle implies 13.9%, about 12.2% net of ordinary volatility. The ATM spread is 40% of mid, so treat that as indicative. Put/call open interest is 0.24, so call-heavy, retail-tilted. The stock is down 92% from its 52-week high of about $42. It ran from about $11 in August to $2.38 on 2026-11-05, as the September lock-up expiry released a resale registration of about 294m Class B shares. It has since bounced 17-21% with the quantum tape after IonQ's raised guide. Short interest is about 8.0m shares, 2.6% of shares outstanding, 0.93 days to cover (stockanalysis, undated). Market cap is about $847m against $312.8m of cash at June 30, so EV is about $594m. Consensus is thin and stale: Q3 revenue about $2.0-2.4m, EPS about -$0.13 (chartmill and stockalarm, undated). Price targets of $29-44 sit 10-15x the price, so the estimates carry no information about the bar. Already public: the Q2 numbers (revenue $1.5m, adjusted EBITDA -$21.3m, capex $6.4m, a guide to accelerating H2 R&D and capex), the Aug 31 roadmap putting meaningful commercialization in 2029-30, the CAD 195m Canada funding (Aug 28), the Bluefors partnership (Sep 29), the GlobalFoundries manufacturing deal (Oct 6-7, +16-17%) and up to $10m of extra DARPA support (Oct 19, the stock fell 7.9% that day). Last earnings reactions: Q1 -10.1%, Q2 -9.3%. This week's peer prints: QBTS -8.6% on its Nov 10 report day, RGTI about -6% today after its Nov 10 amc report.
view: This is a pre-revenue photonic quantum developer that trades on the sector tape, its cash and dilution, and its share-supply overhang, not on the quarter. Revenue is a $1-3m grant line nobody prices. The analyst bar is stale to the point of meaninglessness. Everything material that happened in the quarter was announced by press release before the print: Canada funding, the GlobalFoundries deal, DARPA, Bluefors and the roadmap. What the release can add is the cash balance at Sep 30, my rough estimate of about $280-300m (own arithmetic from the Q2 opex and capex run-rate), any Yorkville ATM draws in Q3 or after quarter end, and spending guidance. Each could cut either way. A disclosed draw at a $3-4 price would be dilutive and bearish. No draw plus a cash balance near a third of the market cap could steady a stock that has fallen 75% in three months. The prior two prints and this week's two small-cap peer prints all sold off 6-10%. That leans the print down, but it is extrapolation from the last reaction, which the playbook warns against, and the 12% implied move already prices a large swing. Selling volume has faded from 30-78m shares a week in Sep-Oct to about 18m and 8.6m, so the forced supply may be largely through. I find no dated datapoint the price does not already hold, and nothing that tells the direction of the open.

recommendation.reason: No mechanism. Every operating event of the quarter is already public, the consensus is too stale to define a surprise, and the reaction will be set by cash and dilution disclosure and by the quantum tape, which I cannot forecast from public data. The slight down-lean rests on how the last two prints and this week's peer prints went, and that is not evidence the price is behind.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A disclosed Yorkville draw at low prices or a cash balance well below about $280m would make the down case. No draws, cash near $300m and a firm DARPA QBI or customer contract in the release would make the up case.

self_critique: The down-lean may be too weak. A stock in a three-month collapse, retail call-heavy, with the two nearest peers sold on their prints, could easily fall again on any dilution hint. Against that, a lean that small cannot justify a trade, and supply exhaustion plus a cash-backed floor argue the other way.
